title: Does shallow alignment depth predict vulnerability to decoding parameter attacks (temperature/top-p manipulation)?

original_idea.problem: The relationship between measured alignment depth (KL metric) and susceptibility to decoding attacks has not been empirically verified across models.
original_idea.direction: For 5-6 small open-weight models with measured alignment depth scores, measure jailbreak ASR under three decoding conditions: greedy, high temperature, and high top-p. Compute Spearman correlation.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If shallow models are disproportionately vulnerable to decoding attacks, this confirms the generality of the shallow alignment explanation beyond prefix/suffix attacks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: shallow alignment -> decoding parameter vulnerability -> validates generality of the shallow alignment framework. Every link is explicit and defensible. Addresses a recognized safety problem (jailbreak vulnerability).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires computing KL divergence curves across multiple models and running inference at various decoding parameters. Standard ML tools but intermediate-level understanding of alignment depth metrics needed. Feasible for beginners with guidance but not trivial.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable: a correlation table between alignment depth and ASR under 3 decoding regimes across 5-6 models. Clear methodology, few dependencies. The broader direction is open but the first result stands alone.

novelty.reasoning: Qi et al. (ICLR 2025) already identified decoding parameter attacks as one manifestation of shallow alignment vulnerability and showed that their deep alignment augmentation reduced decoding exploits from 84.3% to 1.0% ASR. The connection between shallow alignment and decoding parameter vulnerability is established at the conceptual level. The proposed Spearman correlation across 5-6 models adds an empirical quantification not present in Qi et al., who focused on one model's before/after comparison. The incremental contribution is the cross-model correlation analysis, but the core finding is partially known.
